products.name: Publora
products.category: MCP-native social publishing API / agent tooling
products.business_model: Freemium SaaS; free Starter tier, paid from $2.99/account/mo (billed yearly). Per-account pricing scales with connected social accounts.
success_factors: Rode #1 'agent era' positioning — one HTTPS call posts to ~10-12 platforms; MCP server (18 tools) lets agents draft/schedule/reply/analyze
Trust/safety wedge praised in comments: uses official sanctioned platform APIs, NOT scraping or browser automation
Very low $2.99 entry price lowers adoption friction
MCP-native + npx-installable Skills align with Claude/Cursor developer workflows
core_features: Unified publishing API: one call to LinkedIn, X, Instagram, Threads, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Bluesky, Mastodon, Telegram
MCP server with 18 tools for agents to post/comment/react/reply/pull analytics in natural language
Full engagement loop (read feeds, comment, reply to messages)
Official-API-only approach (no scraping)
Google Docs-styled scheduler UI
products.niche: Exposing social publishing as an agent-callable surface rather than a human dashboard
products.audience: Developers, AI agent builders, MCP/automation users (Claude Code, Cursor), content studios, social media managers
products.design: Developer-first, 'agent era' framing; clean MCP-native positioning; Google Docs-style editor for the scheduler
products.reviews: No formal star reviews yet. Positive comment sentiment, especially on official-API safety. Caveat: analytics fully live only for LinkedIn; agent-readiness has room to improve. All figures vendor/PH-stated.

products.name: Spotlight by Backplanes
products.business_model: Free for individuals & their teams (no seats, no trial clock); planned premium enterprise tier (attribution, volume controls, governance) — sales-led, unpriced.
success_factors: Targets the hottest 2026 pain: visibility into what autonomous coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) actually did
Privacy-first (local on-device PII/credential redaction; no OAuth into Anthropic/OpenAI) lowers enterprise fear
Multi-audience reports (engineer, manager, security, finance) broaden the buyer base
Zero-friction 'install once, level up every session' onboarding; free-for-individuals land-and-expand
core_features: Automatic post-session capture (no manual trigger)
Session reports: files touched, commands run, external services reached, scope drift, what deserves review
Security findings: flags credential access & unintended file operations
Multi-audience views (engineering, management, security/CISO, finance/CFO)
Org-level aggregated reports: security posture, capacity, spend
products.niche: The 'what did my agent actually do' audit layer for terminal coding agents
products.audience: Engineers, eng managers (capacity), CISOs (data-access oversight), CFOs (spend/ROI by tool & team)
products.design: Clean, transparency-focused UI; neutral tones; clear report hierarchy. 'See what your agent actually did.'
products.reviews: No formal reviews yet. Strong fit with enterprise governance concerns. Open question: long-term monetization if core stays free.

products.name: ZeroGPU
products.business_model: Usage-based pricing (no public rate card; cost calculator on site). Value prop: 50%+ cost reduction vs frontier models for routine/high-volume work.
success_factors: Drop-in OpenAI-compatible API: swap base URL + model name, minimal migration
Sharp wedge: route high-volume non-reasoning work (classification, moderation, summarization, extraction) off expensive frontier models
Concrete proof point: first customer Dappier runs ~10x lower latency, ~6x lower cost (vendor-stated)
Edge-network + small/nano specialized models + cloud fallback reliability story; rides agent-loop cost anxiety
core_features: OpenAI-compatible chat completions API (drop-in)
Catalog of specialized small/nano models (classification, summarization, PII detection, extraction)
Distributed execution: optimized servers + approved edge devices + cloud fallback
Analytics: cost reduction, latency, avoided frontier-model calls
Project-level API keys / usage-based access
products.niche: Inference cost/efficiency layer for high-volume, repeatable, non-frontier workloads in apps & agent loops
products.audience: Engineering/platform teams at high-volume AI ops: agents, adtech, doc processing, compliance, fraud, moderation
products.design: Minimal infrastructure-credible aesthetic; 'smarter inference over raw compute scaling'
products.reviews: Performance/cost claims are vendor-stated with 'varies by workload' caveat. No customer counts or ARR beyond the single Dappier reference. No independent benchmarks at gather time.

products.name: VC Boom
products.ph: #1 on 2026-06-09, 488 upvotes (highest single-day count of the window)
products.business_model: Free to start; one-time 'pay-once' purchase for access through a raise (no subscription/auto-renew). Positioned to pay for itself from one converting meeting.
success_factors: Highest single-day upvote count of the window (488)
Fast, tangible value: scores a deck in <90s and names the single fastest fix
Large matching dataset: 47,000+ investors, each with a one-line fit rationale
Sends from the founder's own inbox (avoids deliverability/spam stigma of mass tools)
Anti-subscription pay-once pricing aligned with episodic fundraising need
core_features: AI pitch-deck scoring (<90s) with single highest-leverage fix
Investor matching across 47,000+ investors with per-match rationale
Personalized cold-email drafting, sent from user's own inbox
Privacy: Anthropic API, no training on data; encryption at rest
products.niche: Early-stage founders running a raise who need deck feedback + targeted investor outreach in one flow
products.audience: Pre-seed / seed / early-stage founders raising capital
products.design: Conversion-focused, founder-empathetic landing: 'Score your deck. Find investors. Raise.'
products.reviews: Crowded space (cf. Fundraisly). 47,000+ figure and outcome claims vendor-stated; no independent conversion data. Pay-once model differentiates but unproven on repeat-raise value.

products.name: agmsg
products.category: Open-source inter-agent messaging for AI coding agents
products.business_model: Open source / free (GitHub). No commercial model — community/OSS play.
success_factors: Solves a relatable annoyance: manual copy-pasting between AI coding agents
Radically minimal stack: Bash + SQLite only — no daemon, no network, no Python
Vendor-agnostic: works across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI
Installs as an Agent Skill without patching agents
Pre-launch traction in Japan (1M+ impressions, 320+ stars in a week)
core_features: Persistent messaging via a single shared SQLite file (survives sessions)
Vendor-agnostic multi-agent 'rooms' (scales to N agents)
Agent Skill installation (no agent patching)
Zero heavy dependencies
products.niche: Multi-agent orchestration plumbing — heterogeneous coding agents talking directly instead of via human copy-paste
products.audience: Developers running multiple AI coding agents in parallel; agentic-workflow tinkerers
products.design: Developer/OSS minimalism; CLI-first, README-driven, utilitarian hacker brand
products.reviews: Active comment debate on token efficiency, context management, and concurrent SQLite writes (a known SQLite multi-writer weak spot). As OSS with no business model, sustainability is an open question.
